claims.text: server.headersTimeout limits how long the parser waits to receive the complete HTTP headers. Default (Node v24.10.0 docs): the minimum of server.requestTimeout or 60000 ms (since v19.4.0/v18.14.0). Docs say it must be non-zero (e.g. 120 s) to protect against DoS when no reverse proxy is in front.

server.requestTimeout sets the timeout in ms for receiving the entire request from the client. Default 300000 ms (300 s); changed from no timeout in v18.0.0. Docs say it should be non-zero to protect against DoS when no reverse proxy is in front.
When either headersTimeout or requestTimeout expires, the server responds with status 408 without forwarding the request to the request listener, then closes the connection.

server.timeout is the number of ms of socket inactivity before a socket is presumed timed out. Default 0 (no timeout) since v13.0.0 (was 120 s). 0 disables the behavior. It is set up on connection, so changing it affects only new connections, not existing ones.

With server.setTimeout(msecs, callback) or a 'timeout' listener on the Server, the timed-out socket is passed to the listener/callback, and timeouts must then be handled explicitly. Without a listener the Server does not time out sockets by default. The supplied extract does not state what happens to the socket if the listener does nothing, beyond 'must be handled explicitly'.

No. The 300 s default of requestTimeout bounds receiving the entire request from the client (and headersTimeout bounds receiving headers); server.timeout bounds socket inactivity and defaults to 0. None of these is documented as a deadline on application operations (handler work, downstream calls, response generation). Setting them does not prove or enforce a 300 s application-operation deadline. This is an inference from the documented scope of each option; the extract has no statement about handler execution time.

recommendation: Treat headersTimeout and requestTimeout as inbound-request receive limits (408 and connection close, handler never invoked) and server.timeout as a socket inactivity limit (default off). Do not rely on any of them for a 300 s operation deadline. Enforce that separately in application code (e.g. AbortSignal/timers around the operation), and verify behavior by test. Keep headersTimeout and requestTimeout non-zero if no reverse proxy is in front.
unknowns: Only the Node v24.10.0 http.md extract (lines 1828-1960) was used; other docs such as server.keepAliveTimeout, socket-level behavior and the default on-timeout socket handling were not supplied or verified.
The extract does not say whether requestTimeout/headersTimeout expiry applies after the request is dispatched to the listener, beyond the quoted 408 behavior.
